code.originalText: Review two weeks after completing chemoradiation and brachytherapy: side effects, menopause symptoms, and survivorship care

text.paragraph: Review two weeks after completing chemoradiation and brachytherapy. [S]

Ms. Perón returns two weeks after her last brachytherapy treatment. She completed 25 fractions of pelvic radiation and five weekly cisplatin doses without a break, then four brachytherapy treatments, finishing eight weeks after the start. The bladder infection in the third week cleared with nitrofurantoin. The diarrhea settled once radiation ended and she has not needed loperamide for two weeks; nausea stopped after the last cisplatin. She has no bleeding, only a light discharge. For the past ten days she has had about eight hot flashes a day, night sweats that wake her, and vaginal dryness. She has no ringing in the ears or numbness in her hands or feet. She is very tired but walks daily and is working mornings. She has kept seeing the social worker. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1951-05-18; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Thin and tired; weight 50.6 kg; blood pressure 104/66
Mild darkening of the skin in the radiation field; no breakdown
Gentle speculum examination: radiation changes of the upper vagina; cervix smaller, without bleeding; no mass seen

Bleeding after intercourse and between periods, with heavier periods, for about four months, with tiredness and a dull pelvic ache. Never had cervical screening. Speculum examination shows a friable, exophytic mass about 4 cm across on the cervix that bleeds on contact. Punch biopsy, HPV test and cytology taken; urgent gynecologic oncology consultation booked
S — Synthetic presenting problem linked to her documented abnormal bleeding with anemia; superseded by the diagnosis at the consultation.
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss: hemoglobin 9.4 g/dL, mean cell volume 72 fL, ferritin 6 ng/mL, with tiredness and breathlessness on stairs
S — Synthetic modern finding linked to her documented anemia from vaginal bleeding.

Invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, HPV 16 positive: an exophytic tumor about 4.5 cm across with clinical involvement of the left parametrium, not reaching the pelvic wall; pelvic MRI and PET-CT ordered for FIGO 1943 staging. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented cervical cancer
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the gynecologic oncology consultation.

Acute cystitis during pelvic chemoradiation: two days of new burning, urgency and cloudy urine on top of mild radiation frequency, without fever or flank pain; urine dipstick positive for leukocyte esterase and nitrite; culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin; neutrophil count and kidney function normal; resolved
S — Synthetic acute infection; not a historical claim.
Ovarian failure after pelvic radiation, with hot flashes, night sweats, poor sleep and vaginal dryness two weeks after treatment; FSH 72 mIU/mL and estradiol 14 pg/mL
S — Synthetic expected effect of pelvic chemoradiation.

list.item:
Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, FIGO 1943 stage IIB (C53.9). Treatment completed as planned within eight weeks. Acute side effects have settled; no hearing loss or neuropathy after cisplatin; kidney function and magnesium normal (creatinine 0.8 mg/dL, eGFR 101, magnesium 1.9 mg/dL). The tumor already looks smaller. Response is judged by PET-CT and examination about three months after treatment. [S]
PET-CT about three months after treatment.
Vaginal dilator three times a week from now, with a water-based lubricant.
Gynecologic oncology review every three months for two years.

Ovarian failure after pelvic radiation (E89.41). Hot flashes, night sweats and vaginal dryness with FSH 72 mIU/mL and estradiol 14 pg/mL: ovarian failure from pelvic radiation, as she was told to expect. At 32, estrogen therapy relieves symptoms and protects bone and heart; cervical squamous cell carcinoma is not hormone-dependent. Because the uterus remains, a progestogen is added. [S]
Estradiol 0.1 mg patch twice weekly.
Progesterone 100 mg nightly.
Continue until about the usual age of menopause, reviewed yearly.
